instrument.citation: Section 12(2) 118 of former City of Toronto By-law 438-86

calculation_handling.description: Lists the former by-laws and sections that prevail for this exception area: Sections 12(2) 118 and 12(2) 119 of former City of Toronto By-law 438-86 generally, and site-specific by-laws 165-69 (107 Broadway Avenue), 195-67 (15 Erskine Avenue), 20904 (odd 133-141 and 165-171 Erskine Avenue) and 49-02 (even 140-144 Redpath Avenue). These are alternate compliance paths under former by-laws and are never evaluated.
calculation_handling.gaps: The former by-law and section texts are not held, so compliance under them is not checked. The unit text also carries trailing amendment instructions (E)-(N) of By-law 63-2024 that delete or amend other 900.2.10 exceptions; they are not part of exception 912 and are not keyed here.

units.disclosure: This exception lets certain former City of Toronto by-laws and sections (By-law 438-86 Sections 12(2) 118 and 119, and site-specific by-laws for addresses on Broadway Avenue, Erskine Avenue and Redpath Avenue) continue to apply as an alternative way to comply. We do not evaluate compliance under those former by-laws.

900.2.10(912)@63-2024.explanation: By-law 63-2024 rewrote the list of prevailing by-laws for exception 912. Some older City of Toronto rules (Sections 12(2) 118 and 119 of By-law 438-86, and site-specific by-laws for 107 Broadway Avenue, 15 Erskine Avenue, parts of Erskine Avenue and 140-144 Redpath Avenue) can still govern lots in this exception as an alternative to the current zoning by-law. MaxBLD does not check compliance under those older by-laws, so a lot here may have options this analysis does not show.
